description: Review finding CRY-20: Backing up MLS state undermines forward secrecy and risks nonce reuse on restore; the "stateOnly" claim is wrong (lens CRY). Location: spec/02-identity.md:220, spec/02-identity.md:225, spec/02-identity.md:229, spec/02-identity.md:469; vs spec/12-security.md:10. Fix: Drop the nonce-reuse leg. RFC 9420 (rfc9420.txt:1843-1845) says the 4-byte random `reuse_guard` "is used to avoid nonce reuse in the case of state loss or corruption", which is exactly this restore case. The rest stands. A snapshot retains keys that the RFC 9420 §9.2 deletion schedule requires to be deleted, which is a forward-secrecy exception that 12:10 does not mention. Rewound sender generations would in any case be refused by receivers that have already deleted those keys, so "restores MLS continuity" (02:229) is false. A "stateOnly" backup lacks the leaf signature key and cannot send. The exporter (§8.5) derives secrets and does not export state, and RFC 9420 §11 is Group Creation. Fix as proposed: no live ratchet state in backups; rejoin as a new leaf. Full text: notes/review/CRY-verified.md and notes/review/CRY.md.
